summary: Former Rogue River National Forest lookout: a 30-foot L-4 tower from 1934, rebuilt in timber, removed in 1974. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot pole L-4 tower with cab (1934), replaced by a 30-foot treated timber L-4 tower (1953 per the register)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1974. No source describes what remains at the site.

access.note: On Rogue River National Forest land. A 1935 survey sheet notes a road to the top. No source describes current access.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. A 1935 survey sheet says a road reached the top of the ridge.

events.note: 30-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, erected by members of the Camp Applegate CCC
George Ellis, then John Byrne, filled in while J.L. Hoxie was at Oregon National Guard encampments
Forest Service survey description; disk stamped CINNABAR 1935 set in the top of the northwest concrete corner stone of the tower
Earl Potter spent a summer at the lookout
Mrs. Jack Crump spotted a fire from the lookout and reported its location so precisely that fire fighters went straight to it; blaze held to about three quarters of an acre
Aircraft Warning Service station activated August 11, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service station deactivated October 16, 1943; the forest service kept the buildings
30-foot treated timber tower replaced the pole tower (register and Forest Lookouts date)
New 30-foot tower built under the lookout house, which was raised three feet (newspaper, October 1957)
Ike Coffman at his post at the lookout (June 1958)
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, November 24, 2010

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 14 and 16 miles (firelookout.com and the 1935 survey sheet) fit the record's coordinates, roughly 15 miles by a rough check. The 35-mile figure in 1956-57 newspaper notices does not fit and is probably an error.
The register and firelookout.com say pole; the Forest Lookouts page says round timber. Both describe the same 1934 pole-type tower.

notes_for_editor: Two disagreements are not resolved. The treated-timber rebuild is dated 1953 by the register, firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts list, but a 1957 newspaper item describes a new tower built under the house that year. The 1974 removal is 'removed' on the register and Forest Lookouts page and 'destroyed' on firelookout.com. Distance from Medford: 14-16 miles on two sources, 35 miles in newspaper notices. Staffing items are newspaper notices quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; none after June 1958 were found. The 1935 survey disk may or may not survive; no source describes the site today. Record fields (Jackson County, height 9.1 m, status gone) match the sources; no corrections proposed.
